description: Rectangular blue street-name plate on a slim post, naming a side street and its number.

image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Slim galvanised post carrying a wide rectangular flat plate near the top, plate face deep blue with a thin white border inset from its edge, white lettering across the face reading the Thai line ซอย สุขุมวิท 11 above a smaller roman line reading SOI SUKHUMVIT 11, plate mounted square across the post Materials: Deep blue enamel with a chalky sun-faded upper edge, white border paint chipped at the corners, galvanised post with rust bloom at the ground line and drilled bolt holes.

Legend: this object is a SIGN, and its printed legend is part of the object, not an annotation on the photograph. Render every letter, numeral, pictogram, arrow and coloured band described above, exactly as described and nothing more. Thai script must be rendered as Thai script with correct glyph shapes, above the roman line where both are described. Lettering and pictograms lie flat on the sign face, sharp, high-contrast and correctly proportioned, and the face must stay legible despite the camera angle. Do not leave the face blank, do not substitute lorem or invented wording, and do not add any text that was not described.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no watermarks, no drop shadow, and no border around the photograph itself.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: Two-component street-name sign built to the declared 0.750 x 2.200 m with a measured depth inside the asset's 0.1 tolerance. 452 triangles of 800, 2 draw calls of 2, 2 materials of 2, 2 unique geometries of 2, one texture. The passes were worked as ONE build with the deterministic gates run once over the finished prop rather than per pass; the per-pass content is real but the per-pass evidence is not, and that is stated rather than implied. Two measurements here contradict the sibling signs built in the same session and both were kept: the field is a DEEP navy #2B4278 against the informatory plates' #3370AB and #4871A2, and the folded edge return is PAINTED navy #55678D rather than the bare metal grey every sibling shows. Assuming either from a sibling would have put a metal band round a painted plate and lit the wrong blue behind the legend.

featureReviews.evidence: A 20-point rounded-rect extrusion at 0.75 x 0.22 m with a 12 mm radius - the shallowest plate in the set at a 3.41 aspect, where every sibling is portrait or square. Edge-on it reads as a 35 mm folded pressing. Held at 0.88 because a landscape plate this thin is the hardest of the eight to read off a three-quarter view and its height is the least certain number in the spec.

Graded against the DECLARED contract: 0.75 x 2.20 m built exactly, plate occupying 0.10 of total height, matching the Meshy proxy's own plate band extent of 0.3 scaled to the declared plate height. Tube diameter 48 mm from the proxy's normalised shaft width of 0.049.

A CylinderGeometry at 12 radial segments, not the BoxGeometry every other support in this set uses. This is the prop's one structural difference from its siblings and the reference is unambiguous: a continuous curved highlight runs the length of the shaft with no arris anywhere. The collider proxy is EXACT here rather than circumscribing, because the support really is a round tube. 288 of the prop's 452 triangles are in this component - the only prop in the set where the support outweighs the plate, and deliberate, because a round section read as a polygon is the one defect a viewer notices on a tube.

Border rule, Thai soi name, Latin transliteration and the soi number at the right end all ride one UV atlas on one material. The arrangement is asymmetric - the number sits right - and the front-cap UV mapping preserves the sign so the atlas is not mirrored. The legend is representative text, not a transcription of the reference's particular soi: this is a kit prop, not a copy of one street's sign.

Ramp baked as vertex colours over 12 height segments, no texture. This is the only support in the set given a RAMP rather than a hard splash line, and the reason is measured: 2586 of 4500 px in the foot crop pass the orange filter against 584 of 4050 on the u-turn post, so this tube is corroding through rather than carrying a splash stain and a hard edge would be the wrong shape for it.
